prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Below are five specific HVAC companies you should call in the Atlanta area, plus why each is worth contacting and what to ask them. I also include a short checklist of questions and red flags, rough cost ranges, and next steps.

Top companies to call (Atlanta-area)

1) Coolray Heating & Air Conditioning
- Why: Large regional company with many installs in metro Atlanta, offers multiple major brands, financing options, regular maintenance programs, and emergency service. Good option if you want broad availability and quick scheduling.
2) Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta location)
- Why: National chain with local branches; they typically provide written guarantees, factory-authorized dealer status for major brands, and comprehensive maintenance plans. Good for homeowners who want documented warranties and a “comfort club” approach.
3) One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (Metro Atlanta)
- Why: Franchised technicians and guarantees on arrival times; they often have strong local presence and competitive pricing. Useful if you value on-time service and clear, itemized quotes.
4) ARS/Rescue Rooter (Atlanta)
- Why: Large multi-service company offering HVAC, plumbing, and drain services. Good for homeowners who may need combined trades (e.g., ductwork, condensate issues) and want a single company to handle everything.
5) Aire Serv (franchised Atlanta operators)
- Why: Local franchise network that installs many major brands and often provides extended warranties and flexible financing. Good mid-size option that balances local/brand support.

Note: Those are well-known providers that operate in the Atlanta market. In addition to these, it’s a good idea to get at least one quote from an established independent local HVAC contractor (search “best HVAC Atlanta” + check Google Reviews/Yelp/Angi/BBB for top-rated independents in your zip code). Independents sometimes offer lower labor costs and more personalized service.

What to ask every company (must-haves)
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation for proper sizing? (If they don’t, walk away.)
- Which equipment brand and exact model are you quoting (SEER, AFUE, capacity)?
- What is included in the price: equipment, refrigerant, labor, new thermostat, duct modifications, permits, removal/disposal of old unit?
- Written, itemized estimate and timeline (start/end dates).
- Warranty details: manufacturer warranty and company workmanship warranty length.
- Are technicians NATE-certified? Are they licensed and insured? Ask for license number and insurance proof.
- Will you pull required permits and arrange inspections?
- Financing options, rebates, and energy-efficiency incentives (ask if they will apply for local utility or manufacturer rebates for you).
- Maintenance plan options and cost.

Red flags — things to avoid
- Vague quotes (no model numbers or SEER ratings).
- Refusal to do Manual J load calculation.
- Demanding large cash-only deposits or cash discounts off the books.
- No written warranty or refusal to provide proof of insurance/license.
- Extremely low bid well below other estimates (could indicate cut corners or change orders later).

Rough price ranges (ballpark for metro Atlanta)
- Basic replacement of a standard central AC (single-family home): roughly $3,500–$8,000 depending on brand and SEER (good mid-efficiency).
- High-efficiency systems, modifications to ductwork, or upsizing: $8,000–$15,000+.
- These are ballpark ranges; exact price depends on home size, existing ductwork condition, coil/air handler needs, and local labor.

Brands to consider
- Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem, Bryant (depending on budget and installer expertise). Goodman is a lower-cost option with decent value. Ask the contractor why they recommend a particular brand/model for your home.

Utilities & rebates
- Ask contractors about rebates from Georgia Power, local municipal utilities, and manufacturer rebates. Many installers will help submit rebate paperwork.

Next steps I can help with
- If you tell me your Atlanta zip code I can: (a) prioritize local independent contractors in your area and (b) suggest nearby dealer locations for specific brands.  
- If you already have 1–3 written estimates, paste them here and I’ll help compare line items and spot important differences.

Would you like me to narrow these to companies closest to your neighborhood? If so, tell me your zip code or neighborhood.
